Topic.label: The perpendicular segment is shortest and the distance from a point to a line

Question: The perpendicular segment from point \(P\) to line \(l\) has length \(3\) cm. Could the distance from \(P\) to another point \(Q\) on \(l\) be \(2\) cm?

Choices.A: Yes, as long as \(Q\) is close enough to the foot of the perpendicular.
Choices.B: No. The perpendicular segment is the shortest, so \(PQ\) is at least \(3\) cm.
Choices.C: Yes, because \(PQ\) is not necessarily longer than the perpendicular segment.

Solution: Among the segments connecting a point outside a line to points on the line, the perpendicular segment is the shortest, so \(PQ\) cannot be less than \(3\) cm.
